name: Pyrrhus
title: Father of Sopater from Beroea
summary: Pyrrhus is a person mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles as the father of Sopater from Beroea. Sopater was one of Paul's companions on his third missionary journey. Pyrrhus himself plays no independent role in the narrative but is mentioned to identify his son.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as father of Sopater
keyEvents.description: Pyrrhus is mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles as the father of Sopater from Beroea, who accompanied Paul on his journey from Greece back to Asia.

keyEvents.title: Sopater among Paul's companions
keyEvents.description: His son Sopater was among those who accompanied Paul through Macedonia as part of a group of believers from several congregations.

keyEvents.title: The companions' stay in Troas
keyEvents.description: The group that included Sopater, son of Pyrrhus, traveled ahead to Troas and waited there for Paul and Luke.

keyEvents.title: Connection to the congregation in Beroea
keyEvents.description: Pyrrhus likely belonged to the Jewish or Christian community in Beroea, a city known for its inhabitants who examined the Scriptures daily after Paul's preaching there.
